notes: Batch D (metformin, levothyroxine, omeprazole, sertraline, St John's wort). All quotes taken from fetchtext output and checked with --check. BNF/BNFC not accessed (geo-blocked). CONFLICTS RECORDED AS SEPARATE ITEMS/RULES: (1) Metformin breastfeeding - Glucophage SmPC says breastfeeding 'is not recommended'; SPS says metformin 'can be used during breastfeeding' (preferred choice, with infant monitoring). (2) Sertraline breastfeeding - Lustral SmPC 'not recommended unless...benefit outweighs the risk'; SPS names sertraline an SSRI of choice. (3) Sertraline pregnancy - SmPC 'not recommended in pregnancy, unless...'; BUMPS says SSRIs are commonly taken in pregnancy and stopping can cause relapse. (4) Levothyroxine tablets (Eltroxin) vs oral solution (ADVANZ 100 micrograms/5 ml) section 4.3 differ: tablets list thyrotoxicosis and 'adrenal gland disorder or adrenal insufficiency' as contraindications; the oral solution lists 'adrenal insufficiency without adequate corticosteroid cover' and does not list thyrotoxicosis in 4.3 (its 4.4 says levothyroxine should not be given in hyperthyreotic states except as supplementation during anti-thyroid treatment). Both kept, per formulation. (5) Metformin IR vs SR renal table: maximum daily dose for GFR 60-89 mL/min is 3000 mg (IR) vs 2000 mg (SR); both SmPCs give GFR in 'mL/min' (not eGFR/CrCl) - kept as 'GFR'. (6) St John's wort: two THR SPCs (Hyperiforce, THR 13668/0014; Kira LowMood Relief, THR 43546/0001) have different extracts and doses (one tablet three times daily vs one tablet daily); Kira 4.3 adds soya/peanut allergy and states the product 'should not be taken concomitantly with the medicines included in section 4.5'. St John's wort SPCs were read from the MHRA Products document store (mhraproducts4853.blob.core.windows.net, the PDF files that products.mhra.gov.uk links to); the products.mhra.gov.uk search page itself is JavaScript-rendered and returns no text. ITEMS NOT FOUND / LEFT OUT: no SPS breastfeeding page found for omeprazole/PPIs or levothyroxine (SmPC 4.6 used); no BUMPS leaflet for levothyroxine or St John's wort; no SPS monitoring page for metformin, omeprazole or sertraline (404); UKTIS monographs not used. St John's wort THR SPC lists 'Oral hypoglycaemic drugs: Gliclazide' - metformin is not named, so no St John's wort-metformin rule was made. Metformin SmPC lists trimethoprim as an OCT2 inhibitor; co-trimoxazole is not named, so no co-trimoxazole rule. GROUP MEMBERSHIP NEEDED FROM OTHER BATCHES (referenced here but members not sourced by batch D): nsaid, ace-inhibitor, diuretic, antihypertensive, corticosteroid, opioid, anticoagulant, antiplatelet, qt-prolonging, antacid. MHRA DSU 'Antidepressants: new safety measures...' was published 15 October 2026 (very recent) - sertraline is named in its footnote list. Brand-specific prescribing: no UK source says to prescribe levothyroxine by brand routinely; MHRA (2021) says generic prescribing remains appropriate for most patients but to consider consistently prescribing a specific well-tolerated product if a patient is persistently symptomatic after switching. SECOND-CHECK AUDIT 2026-10-17 (details in audit/D.md): metformin renal 30-44 'starting dose at most half' confirmed (the emc table cell spans the 45-59 and 30-44 rows, ROWSPAN=2). Kira LowMood Relief (THR 43546/0001) puts its whole 4.5 table under 4.3 Contraindications, so product-specific 'contraindicated' rules were added for the master-list medicines in that table; Hyperiforce (THR 13668/0014) rules stay 'avoid'. Added sources sps-heartburn-breastfeeding and sps-qt-commonly-used (same ids and URLs as batches G and E). SPS (QT page) says sertraline has no QTc effect at licensed doses, which differs from the Lustral SmPC; both kept. The co-trimoxazole case is covered: metformin's trimethoprim rule matches co-trimoxazole through its trimethoprim ingredient.
